name: Incline Dumbbell Biceps Curl
grip: Supinated, palms facing forward at the bottom and upward as the elbows bend.
description: Curl two dumbbells while reclining on an incline bench, keeping the upper arms hanging beside the torso.
setup: Set the backrest to a comfortable incline, approximately 45-60 degrees above horizontal.
Sit with the back supported and feet flat, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Let the arms hang beside the bench with palms forward and elbows softly extended.
instructions: Bend both elbows to curl the dumbbells toward the shoulders.
Keep the upper arms hanging rather than swinging them forward.
Pause before the shoulders lift from the bench.
Lower slowly toward the starting position without forcing elbow or shoulder extension.
cues: Keep the back on the support.
commonMistakes: Swinging the upper arms forward to finish.
Arching away from the backrest or forcing a deep shoulder stretch.

logging.example: Two 12 kg dumbbells: record 12 kg per dumbbell.
logging.note: Keep the same exercise variant and record each dumbbell's mass rather than the combined pair.

variantNote: Seated incline, both arms curling together with palms supinated. The illustration uses about a 50-degree backrest; keep bench angle consistent.
reviewNotes: Confirm preferred bench angle and simultaneous rather than alternating execution.
The far arm is partly occluded in the illustration's lowered pose; the written version uses two dumbbells.
